criteria.criterion: Run cargo test: a fixture-record test shows each of the three evidence kinds (retry outcome, recurrence after prevention, critic/verifier same-cause findings) yielding a class-label with evidence-derived labeler and a basis citing the record ids it rests on.
criteria.evidence: All 13 tests passed. Each evidence kind has its own fixture test, and each asserts the kind and the cited ids: a_retry_that_followed_the_proposed_request_and_landed_gives_a_label_citing_it (Labeler::Evidence; the basis cites the introspection and the retry job), athena_retry_of_the_job_counts_and_a_retry_failing_for_the_same_cause_gives_a_label (cites the retry's own introspection), a_class_that_kept_recurring_or_stopped_after_a_prevention_landed_gives_labels (cites the proposal record, the applying job and the recurrence), and critic_and_independent_verifier_findings_that_name_the_cause_give_a_label. The CLI test derive_writes_evidence_labels_with_their_basis_once_and_scores_them checks 32 written labels, each with a retry-outcome basis.

criteria.criterion: Run cargo test: a fixture introspection with no evidence gets no label and counts as unlabeled.
criteria.evidence: a_case_with_no_evidence_gets_no_label_and_is_counted_as_unlabeled passed: no_evidence is 1, derived is 0, and labeled::build reports the case as unreviewed. In the CLI test, case 200 is left unlabeled (no_evidence 1, excluded.unreviewed 1). derive_with_no_evidence_reports_zero_labels_and_no_verdict_and_commits_nothing passed.

criteria.criterion: Run cargo test: when both a person label and an evidence label exist for one introspection, the person label is used by the labeled set, whichever is newer; and derivation never edits or deletes an existing record, and rerunning does not duplicate labels.

findings.summary: Reruns after new jobs close append new copies of the recurrence labels, because their basis text includes a job count
findings.evidence: A rerun skips a case only when an evidence label with the same class and the same basis already exists. The recurrence-after-prevention detail embeds `did not recur over {closed} jobs` or `recurred in {n} later introspections`, and those numbers change as jobs close. So each later --derive run appends a fresh evidence label for every such case, with the same class and new wording. An immediate rerun writes nothing, as tested. D137 discloses this behavior ('if the evidence changed, a newer evidence label is appended'), but the records will grow with every run.

summary: The change adds `athena score-jev --derive`. It reads the records and appends `athena.class-label/1` records marked `labeled_by: evidence`. Each label carries a `basis` that cites the record ids it rests on, from three kinds of later evidence: the retry's outcome, whether the class recurred after a prevention landed, and critic or verifier findings that name the same cause. Cases with no evidence, or with evidence that names different classes, stay unlabeled. A label from a person or a stronger model beats an evidence label even when the evidence label is newer. score-jev now reports how many counting labels came from evidence, split by kind. I ran the targeted tests and all passed: 13 for evidence labels and precedence, 2 CLI integration tests (they check that the new commit only adds class-label files, that a rerun writes nothing, and that a review overrides an evidence label), and the schema round-trip test. Athena's recorded fmt, clippy and test checks also passed. I ran score-jev read-only on this snapshot. It has no records/, so it reported 0 derived labels and a shortfall with no verdict. That is a result about the snapshot only. Nobody has yet run `score-jev --derive` on the real repository's records: not the producer (D137 says so) and not me (the snapshot holds no records, and the flag would write commits). So the number of derived labels and any real score or verdict are still unknown until it is run after landing. Minor findings: 4 files changed outside the deliverables list, all supporting changes. Labels citing recurrence-after-prevention evidence include a job count in their basis, and that count changes as jobs close, so later reruns append fresh copies of those labels.
